questions.question: What is the smallest positive integer n such that n is divisible by both 12 and 18 and leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 25?

options.explanation: This does not satisfy the remainder condition when divided by 25.
This does not satisfy the remainder condition when divided by 25.
This satisfies both the divisibility conditions and the remainder condition when divided by 25.
This does not satisfy the remainder condition when divided by 25.

questions.explanation: The LCM of 12 and 18 is 36. So, n = 36k. We need 36k ≡ 3 (mod 25). Solving 36k ≡ 3 (mod 25), we get 11k ≡ 3 (mod 25). The modular inverse of 11 modulo 25 is 16, so k ≡ 3 × 16 ≡ 48 ≡ 23 (mod 25). Thus, k = 23 gives the smallest n = 36 × 23 = 828. However, checking smaller values, k = 1 gives n = 183, which satisfies all conditions.

questions.explanation: If n has the prime factorization n = p_1^a_1 p_2^a_2 ... p_k^a_k, then n^2 = p_1^(2a_1) p_2^(2a_2) ... p_k^(2a_k). The number of divisors is (2a_1 + 1)(2a_2 + 1) ... (2a_k + 1), which is always odd. Thus, the number of positive divisors of n^2 is always odd.
